hook: Stars wrapped around a negative-mass core can be stable and more compact than regular polytropes.
summary: Solving the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations gives shells around a negative-mass singularity, called singustars. Radial mode analysis finds stable ones for Gamma = 2 up to compactness about 0.25, and nonlinear runs show collapse or dispersal depending on the perturbation. These are theoretical objects, and negative mass is not known to exist.
title: Singustars: Between Black Holes and Compact Stars
